terminal.emulator: direct PTY with rendered screen model and loopback HTTP fixture

reference.capture: fresh synthetic Hermes home with a no-selection control, bounded Enter selection, and fresh-process readback

normalization: Reference checkout, synthetic HOME/HERMES_HOME paths, session identifiers, timestamps, raw redraw bytes, and dynamic cache contents are omitted or represented by stable markers.
The local HTTP fixture records only method/path, content type, body size, and whether the synthetic configured header was present; no request payload or credential value is stored.
Config bytes are compared as changed/unchanged with sanitized lengths and hashes in the generated runtime report; file output is reduced to artifact-root classes and counts.

The no-selection control separates Hermes startup/config/cache initialization from effects observed after Enter on the visible model row; repeated metadata probes are recorded as reference diagnostics, not a Hades compatibility requirement.

unknowns: Whether Enter changes the effective model beyond the transient model status marker is not proven without a distinct model or a subsequent isolated chat request.
Persistence toggles, alternate model rows, empty inventories, unreachable providers, authentication failures, and selection across sessions remain unobserved.
The observed repeated metadata requests may be provider discovery behavior or a reference failure boundary; Hades must not reproduce them without separate evidence.
